result.reasoning:
REFUTED on both substance and materiality. The mechanical fact (85 signs change between s2 and s3, 19 fall from >+1.5 to <0) reproduces exactly, but the three claims that make it a defect are all false.

1. THE ROOT-CAUSE STORY IS WRONG — sign=-1 is not "the mirror of the correct book". Measured on the real operator (tmp/review/refute-signlock-mirror/m3_semantics.py, synthetic 1000-name panel, partura.ops_ext.cs_first_high40 + alphacube.metrics.long_short_weights): the sign=+1 book holds 100.0% of its names INSIDE the selected top-40%-of-x segment; the sign=-1 book holds 0.0% inside it; the two books share 0 of 100 names. The sign=-1 book also shares 0 of 100 names with the semantically intended neg(y)-inside book. So sign=-1 is a third, different book — "trade the COMPLEMENT segment with y inverted" — not the mirror of the intended one. The lock therefore did not report a +2.6 candidate as -2.8; s2's +2.646 was never a reading of h_sieve_known as written. The code comment at sweep.py:139-141 describes exactly the inversion it prevents, and the lock does prevent it.

2. NOTHING VANISHED FROM THE RECORD, AND THE RECORDED CONCLUSION ALREADY REJECTED THESE CANDIDATES AT THEIR BEST READING — runs/<fid>/sweepfinal_s2.json exists and is ledgered for all 15 factors; it read the "lost" candidates on the holdout under their unlocked sign=-1 books: F102 seg_new_p +6.35%/+1.15, F102 h_sieve_known +14.04%/+1.56, F109 h_e_spine_high40 +5.68%/+0.57. And the write-up states the verdict from those s2 numbers — /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/handoff/F102_kurt_autocorr/STATE.md:56: "h_sieve_known(+16.3%/2.65) ... 比通用筛子基准 k_known_xfrozen(+18.5%/3.15)低 0.5 以上夏普 —— 升华失败、在已知族之上冗余". The claim "扫描日志里它看起来是一条被证伪的假设" does not match the record.

3. NOT ONE of the 85 flipped expressions beats the benchmark the rule judges this family against, even at its best (unlocked) reading — k_known_xfrozen = +3.154 utrain pure-long Sharpe, byte-identical in every run and unaffected by the lock (its y is already neg(KNOWN)). Max over all 85 = +2.669; only 9 of 85 beat even bare k_known (+2.224). So the lock cannot have removed anything that would change a conclusion.

4. ZERO REPORTED NUMBERS CHANGE — of the fusion legs in runs/_batch_B01/fuse_s2.json (38 members) and fuse_s3.json (41 members), 0 have a sign the lock changed. Every screen/segment variant that actually reached a fusion already had sign=+1 at s2, i.e. was already direction-aligned, so the lock is a no-op on all of them. The headline (research/alpha_distillation/B01_upgrades_and_fusion.md:12,121 — 9 independent legs equal-weight, in-sample +20.1%/Sharpe 3.99, out-of-sample +15.7%/Sharpe 1.88) is built entirely from untouched legs.

5. THE ONE LOCK-AFFECTED VARIANT THAT REACHED A REPORTED TABLE WAS WORTH NOTHING — F102.seg_new_p is a leg of `indep_eq` in the s2 summary (research/alpha_distillation/B01_batch_summary.md:93, +20.1%). That report's own leave-one-out (line 105): removing it gives +20.3%/+3.74 vs +20.1%/+3.81 with it, i.e. contribution -0.1% net excess / +0.07 Sharpe — negative in return terms and an order of magnitude inside the ±0.3 Sharpe / ±3pp noise band.

6. THE REMOVED INFORMATION IS A MARKET EFFECT THE RESEARCH ALREADY CAPTURED, BETTER — the complement-segment book is listing-age/liquidity, not a factor finding: at s2, seg_hiliq_p had sign=-1 for 15/15 factors, mean +1.41 Sharpe (sd 0.92), and seg_new_p mean +0.94 — factor-independent (m1_segment_vs_factor.py). The team had already documented this: handoff/TOOLING.md:57 records that seg_new_p's real holding in the new-stock segment is 0 ("两者的真实持仓都是 0"), and B01_reverse_guidance.md:51 catalogues seg_new_p as the generic motif "把上市最短的四成排到最后" across 15 factors. The s3 round re-expressed it directly as h3_age_bucket, which dominates seg_new_p in and out of sample (utrain +2.93/holdout +1.24 vs +2.67/+1.15), and the s3 overlays beat the "lost" s2 overlay on both splits (h3_xfroz_max60 +3.11/+1.60 and h3_max60_ov05 +2.81/+1.78 vs h_sieve_known +2.65/+1.56). The s3 fusion lands on the same +20.1% in-sample as the s2 fusion that included seg_new_p.

Net: the lock is a semantics fix that does its stated job, it changed no reported number and no reported conclusion, and the only affected leg that reached a reported table contributed -0.1pp / +0.07 Sharpe. Severity "high" is not supportable; this is at most a forward-looking grid-coverage note.

result.corrected_fix: No correction is needed to anything already reported — do not re-run or restate the s2/s3 numbers. As a forward-looking grid-coverage note only (not a defect): keep the lock exactly as it is at scripts/sweep.py:142 and adopt only the reporter's option (b) — in `variants()`, for every cs_first_*/cs_last_*-rooted expression whose first argument is not already `neg(...)` (notably --extra and propose output), auto-add a twin with y replaced by `neg(y)`, so both y-directions enter the grid under sign=+1. That is what the comment at sweep.py:108-109 ("Both directions, since the sign is only known after scoring") intends. Reject the reporter's option (a): releasing the lock when the first argument is not syntactically `neg(...)` re-opens the exact inversion the lock exists to stop, and it re-opens it precisely on the hand-written hypotheses that need it most — h_sieve_known's y is `cs_rank(cross_mean(day_std(Amt), 30))`, not `neg(...)`, so (a) would hand the sign back to the rank IC, which picks -1 and silently relabels a complement-segment book as "a sieve on the known family". If this twin is added, note that the complement-segment direction it does NOT cover (sign=-1's "trade everything outside the segment") is a market-wide listing-age/liquidity effect, already captured cleanly and better by h3_age_bucket / cross_age-style variants; expressing it as a segment operator with an inverted sign is what produced the factor-independent +0.9 to +1.4 Sharpe readings across all 15 factors in s2.
